stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Grab the mirror and rotate it. Watch the orange beam bounce — the two angles around the dotted normal always stay equal.
stages.concept: Law of reflection: $\theta_i = \theta_r$ — the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Aim the mirror, then press Fire (or Space) to shoot the beam. Light all 3 stars — you have 7 shots.
stages.concept: You aim only by controlling the mirror's angle.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The beam is invisible. Read the coordinates of $S$, $M$ and $T$, compute the mirror angle $\varphi$ that sends the beam onto the target, set the mirror, then Fire. Peek reveals your current $\varphi$ so you can verify your calculation.
stages.concept: The mirror is perpendicular to the bisector of the angle formed by $\overrightarrow{MS}$ and $\overrightarrow{MT}$.

labels.exhausted: OUT OF SHOTS · RESET TO RETRY
labels.tip2: aim, then press SPACE to fire
labels.tip3: compute φ from coordinates, then fire

1.1: Grab the mirror by its endpoints and rotate it slowly.
1.2: The dotted line is the normal — perpendicular to the mirror at its pivot.
1.3: Watch the two arcs: the beam and its reflection make equal angles with the normal.

2.1: The beam only fires when you press Fire (or Space). Aim first.
2.2: Rotating the mirror by X° rotates the reflected beam by 2X°.
2.3: For each star: orient the mirror so its perpendicular bisects the angle from source-to-mirror and mirror-to-star.

3.1: You need to compute the mirror angle from the coordinates. Read S, M and T from the scene.
3.2: Compute the direction from M to S: α₁ = atan2(S.y − M.y, S.x − M.x). Do the same for T: α₂ = atan2(T.y − M.y, T.x − M.x).
3.3: The mirror angle is φ = (α₁ + α₂)/2 − 90°. Set it, Peek to verify, then Fire.
